Control your **VIZIO SmartCast TVs and sound bars** from Gladys, on your local network: power,
volume, mute, inputs, apps, picture and sound modes, remote keys. No cloud, no VIZIO account: Gladys
talks to the SmartCast API of each device directly (the API the VIZIO mobile app uses).

> Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome. This integration was written from the
> documented protocol and from real answers of VIZIO TVs published by open-source projects, not
> tested on a real TV yet. Tell us what works and what does not:
> [github.com/guim31/gladys-vizio/issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-vizio/issues).

This integration is not affiliated with VIZIO, Inc. VIZIO and SmartCast are trademarks of their
owners.

## Prerequisites

- A VIZIO **SmartCast** TV (2016 and later) or sound bar, on the same local network as Gladys.
- Gladys Assistant **5.1.0** or later.
- On the TV, set the power mode to **Quick Start** (Menu, System, Power Mode). In **Eco Mode**, a
  TV in standby turns its network off: Gladys can neither see it nor turn it on, until it is turned
  on with its remote. The integration does not use Wake-on-LAN: VIZIO does not document it, and
  no report shows it waking a TV in Eco Mode.
- Give each device a fixed IP address in your router (recommended).

## Installation and configuration

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, then **Install from GitHub**, and install
   `guim31/gladys-vizio`.
2. Turn your TVs and sound bars on. The integration looks for them on the network (mDNS, through
   Gladys) when it starts and at each **Search** in the Discovery tab.
3. A device that is not found (another network, mDNS blocked): type its IP address in **Addresses
   (optional)**, several separated by commas (`192.168.1.30, 192.168.1.31`).
4. Sound bars need no pairing: they show up in the Discovery tab at once. TVs must be paired first
   (below).
5. In the **Discovery** tab, add the devices to Gladys.

Options:

- **Favorite apps**: the apps offered in the **App** list of each TV and by default in the
  shortcuts widget, by their SmartCast name (`Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, Apple
TV+` by default, 12 at most). The names are those of the SmartCast catalog of pyvizio (150 apps:
  Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, YouTube, YouTube TV, Max as "HBO Max", Peacock, Paramount+,
  Plex, Pluto TV, Tubi, Apple TV+…); a name not in the catalog is reported in the integration
  status.
- **Refresh interval**: 10, 15 or 30 seconds.
- **Volume step**: change of each press on Volume + and Volume −.
- **Language of the feature names**: the names given to the features when a device is added (they
  stay as they are afterwards), and the texts of the lists and of the scene events. French by
  default.

### Pairing a TV

A TV only obeys a client it knows: it shows a PIN, and gives a token once the PIN is typed. The
integration keeps the token in its private storage (`/data`), never in the logs.

1. Turn the TV on.
2. In the configuration of the integration, run **Start pairing**. The TV shows a 4-digit PIN. With
   several TVs waiting for pairing, type the address of the one to pair in the action field.
3. Type the PIN in the field of **Enter the PIN** and run it, within 5 minutes.
4. The TV appears in the Discovery tab: add it.

The TV lists Gladys among its paired devices (named "Gladys"). A wrong PIN can be typed again while
the TV still shows it. Pairing again replaces the token. After a factory reset of the TV, pair it
again.

**Test the connection** looks for the devices, reads each of them, and tells for each what it
finds: model, on or in standby, Eco mode, pairing needed, an address that does not answer.

## Devices and features

One device per TV or sound bar, identified by its serial number: a change of IP address (DHCP) is
followed, the device stays the same.

### TV

| Feature           | What it does                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Power             | On or standby; turns the TV on or off (Quick Start mode needed to turn it on).        |
| Volume            | 0 to 100, as on the TV.                                                               |
| Volume down / up  | Buttons, by the volume step of the configuration.                                     |
| Mute              | Button: mutes or unmutes (the state is shown by the widget and Now playing).          |
| Input             | List of the TV's inputs, with the names set on the TV (SmartCast, HDMI-1, PS5…).      |
| App               | SmartCast Home, the favorite apps, and "Other" (an input, or an app not in the list). |
| Now playing       | Text: the app (Netflix…), the input, or Off.                                          |
| Picture mode      | List of the picture modes of the TV (Vivid, Calibrated, Game…), when it has them.     |
| Channel down / up | Buttons, on TVs with a tuner.                                                         |

### Sound bar

Power, Volume (0 to 31 on most sound bars, read from the device), Volume down, Volume up, Mute,
Input (HDMI, Bluetooth, optical…), Now playing (the input), and **Sound mode** (the EQ of the sound
bar: Music, Movie…) when it has one.

The feature names follow the **Language of the feature names** option: Power, Volume, Volume down,
Volume up, Mute, Input, App, Now playing, Picture mode, Sound mode, Channel down, Channel up.

## Dashboard widgets

- **VIZIO remote**: state of the device, what is playing, volume, and the Power, Volume −, Volume +
  and Mute buttons.
- **VIZIO shortcuts**: four favorite apps or inputs, opened in one tap; the TV turns on first if
  needed. Type their names in the widget settings (`Netflix`, `HDMI-1`, `PS5`); all empty: the
  favorite apps of the configuration (the inputs on a sound bar). The one in front shows a check
  mark.
- **VIZIO keys**: four remote keys of your choice (arrows by default; add a second widget for OK,
  Back, Home, Menu…). A sound bar only has some of them.

Each widget follows one device, chosen in its settings (the first one when empty).

## Scene trigger

**TV: app or input changed** fires when something new is in front, turning on included: an app
(Netflix, YouTube…) or an input (a console over HDMI). Filters: the device, the kind (app or input)
and the name, exactly as shown by the **Now playing** feature (`Netflix`, `HDMI-1`, `PS5`). It is
seen within the refresh interval. Variables: the device name, the kind (`app` or `input`) and the
name.

Power on and off need no trigger: use the state of the **Power** feature.

## Scene actions

- **Open an app on the TV**: by its SmartCast name (`Netflix`, `Prime Video`, "disney plus" works
  too). Turns the TV on first if needed. Returns the name of the app opened.
- **Choose an input**: by its name or the name set on the TV (`HDMI-1`, `PS5`). Turns the device
  on first if needed.
- **Send a remote control key**: arrows, OK, Back, Home, Menu, Info, Play, Pause, Rewind, Fast
  forward, Volume, Mute, Channel, Last channel, Next input; repeated up to 10 times.

## Scene examples

- **Movie night**: trigger **TV: app or input changed**, kind App, name `Netflix` → dim the living
  room lights to 20 % and close the shutters.
- **Game time**: trigger **TV: app or input changed**, kind Input, name `PS5` → set the picture
  mode to Game (feature Picture mode) and turn the ambient light on.
- **Good night**: at 11:30 pm, if the TV **Power** is on → send a notification, then turn the TV off
  15 minutes later.
- **Wake-up news**: at 7 am on weekdays → **Open an app on the TV** `YouTube TV`, then set the
  volume to 15.

## Refresh and network use

The integration reads each device on its own timer, at the chosen interval: one request for the
power state of a TV in standby; when it is on, two to four requests (power, input and app, sound
settings, picture mode). A device that does not answer (Eco mode) costs one connection attempt per
interval, and is not shown as an error. The states are sent to Gladys only when they change, and
again every 6 hours. The inputs are read again every 30 minutes, the bounds and lists of the
settings once a day.

The SmartCast API is local, without quota; its server is small, so the integration sends one
request at a time to each device. Everything stays on your network: HTTPS on port 7345 or 9000,
with the self-signed certificate of the device.

## Troubleshooting

- **No device found**: the device must be on (or in Quick Start standby) and on the same network as
  Gladys. Otherwise, type its address in **Addresses (optional)**, then run **Test the
  connection**.
- **"Pairing needed"** in the integration status: run **Start pairing** with the TV on.
- **"The TV no longer accepts Gladys"**: the TV forgot the token (factory reset, firmware update):
  pair it again.
- **The TV does not turn on from Gladys**: it is in Eco Mode; choose Quick Start on the TV.
- **Wrong PIN**: type the PIN shown again, or run **Start pairing** again for a new one. After too
  many tries, the TV refuses pairing for a while.
- **An app does not open, or shows as "Unknown app"**: it is not in the SmartCast catalog, or its
  identifier changed. Tell us its name in an issue.
- **Detailed logs**: start the container with `LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

## Limitations

- Developed without the hardware: the requests follow pyvizio and vizaio, and the captures of a
  real TV they published, but this integration has not run against a real VIZIO device yet.
- A TV in Eco Mode cannot be seen nor turned on while in standby.
- The list of apps is the SmartCast catalog of pyvizio: a TV has no request listing its installed
  apps.
- The mute state is shown, but Mute is a toggle button (SmartCast TVs treat every mute key as a
  toggle).
- Picture mode and Sound mode depend on the firmware: they appear only when the device offers them.
- VIZIO sells SmartCast devices in North America only.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings VIZIO SmartCast asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your VIZIO devices | `section` | No | SmartCast TVs and sound bars are found on your network. Pair each TV once with the two actions below. Set the TV power mode to Quick Start: in Eco mode, Gladys cannot turn it on. |
| Addresses (optional) | `string` | No | Only for a device the search does not find: its IP address, separated by commas. Give it a fixed address in your router. |
| Favorite apps | `string` | No | The apps of the App list of each TV and of the shortcuts widget, by their SmartCast name, separated by commas (12 at most). |
| Options | `section` | No |  |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often the devices are read. A device in Eco mode is not read. |
| Volume step | `select` | No | Change of each press on Volume + and Volume −. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features when a device is added, and texts of the lists and scene events. |

## How to install VIZIO SmartCast in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: VIZIO SmartCast appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-vizio:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-vizio](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-vizio).

VIZIO SmartCast requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
